description: Simulates continuous-time analog signals as dense discrete arrays. Ground-truth source for all Ch.4 experiments. Signals generated from explicit trigonometric formulas.
problem_motivation: Computers cannot store continuous-time signals x_c(t). To analyze sampling without physical hardware, we construct an ultra-dense discrete grid at F_ANALOG >> 2*f_max to act as continuous ground truth.
knowns: Continuous signal formulas x_c(t) = A*cos(2*pi*f0*t + phi); Target band limit f_max; Sampling grid step Ts = 1/fs.
unknowns: Values at non-grid timestamps; Reconstruction error under downsampling.
assumptions: Dense reference rate F_ANALOG (100 kHz) approximates continuous time with numerical error < 1e-8, serving as valid ground truth.
mathematical_model: t = [0 : 1/F_ANALOG : T]; x_dense = x_c(t); x_sampled[n] = x_dense[n * M] where M = F_ANALOG / fs.
